gaps.sentence: There was a lot of ___ (OPPOSE) to the new road.
gaps.explanation: 'A lot of' needs a noun: opposition (-tion noun); 'opposite' is an adjective or noun meaning the contrary.

gaps.sentence: The vaccine is still awaiting official ___ (APPROVE).
gaps.explanation: 'Official approval' — the noun form follows the adjective.

gaps.sentence: His ___ (CONFIDENT) was shaken by the failure.
He felt he was ___ for the work he did, so he asked for a raise (PAY).
gaps.hint: paid too little — he wants a raise (under-)
gaps.explanation: The prefix under- means too little: underpaid means paid less than deserved, which explains asking for a raise.

gaps.sentence: The ___ (DEEP) of the lake is still unknown.
He had a happy ___ in the countryside (CHILD).
gaps.hint: noun needed: the period of being a child (-hood)
gaps.explanation: The suffix -hood forms period-of-life nouns: childhood.

gaps.sentence: She was praised for her ___ (TOLERATE) of other viewpoints.
We had a ___ view of the coast from the plane (SPECTACLE).
gaps.explanation: The adjective of 'spectacle' is spectacular; it modifies the noun 'view'.
